applicable_when: The kernel is a transpose/permutation over xnumel=9 and ynumel=13312. The current launch uses XBLOCK=128 but xnumel=9, meaning 119 of 128 threads per block are masked out (xmask=False) and do zero useful work. This wastes ~93% of thread slots in the X dimension. With only 0.79 waves/SM the grid is too small to saturate the H200's 132 SMs. The result is 54% achieved occupancy vs 100% theoretical, and 43.82% of scheduler cycles with no eligible warp. Fixing XBLOCK to match xnumel=9 (use XBLOCK=16 to cover 9 with minimal waste) and increasing YBLOCK to compensate for the smaller X tile will produce more CTAs, better occupancy, and more coalesced access. Adding @triton.autotune explores the best combination automatically.

applicable_when: The kernel is a transpose/permutation over shape (32, 416, 3, 3). xnumel=9 (the 3x3 spatial dimension) and ynumel=13312 (32x416). The current XBLOCK=128 is catastrophically oversized for xnumel=9 — only 9 of 128 threads in the X dimension do real work, wasting 93% of thread slots in every CTA. This produces only 1 CTA in the X grid dimension (cdiv(9,128)=1) and 1664 in Y, giving 0.79 waves/SM on a 132-SM GPU. Reducing XBLOCK to match xnumel (e.g., XBLOCK=1 or XBLOCK=4) and increasing YBLOCK (e.g., 16, 32, 64) will: (1) eliminate wasted threads, (2) increase the number of CTAs and waves/SM, (3) improve L1 cache reuse on the Y dimension, and (4) reduce the occupancy gap. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the optimal combination.
